    Global Update: Pope Leo XIV returns after lung cancer surgery

    Ella Kang, Staff Writer • October 29, 2026
    Jaewon Jang
    After a surgical procedure for lung cancer, Pope Leo XIV returns to Apostolic Palace, Vatican on Oct. 17. Post-lung adenocarcinoma diagnosis, a subtype of lung cancer, the Pope underwent a surgery of removing the lower lobe of his lung on Oct. 13 at Agostino Gemelli Hospital in Rome.

    Editor’s note: Maria wishes to keep her last name undisclosed.

    Pope Leo XIV returned to Apostolic Palace, Vatican on Oct. 17 after a surgical procedure for lung cancer. Post lung adenocarcinoma diagnosis, a subtype of lung cancer, the Pope underwent a surgery of removing the lower lobe of his lung on Oct. 13 at Agostino Gemelli Hospital in Rome. 

    On Oct.21, the Vatican announced that the cancer had shrunk and that no further cancer treatment was necessary. Despite these clinical results, the Pope is still recovering from surgery, so doctors continue to recommend precautions in his daily life. 

    “He just ascended to papacy … it would have been tragic for him to hear … [about] getting diagnosed with cancer … [soon] after … [being elected as a pope],” Maria, a Catholic who works as a Spanish teacher, said.

    Story continues below advertisement

    Maria believes the Pope’s recovery is a meaningful moment for Catholics and one that amplifies her faith. 

    “As a Catholic, I always believe that prayer can give us strength and hope during miserable times,” Maria said. “Hearing that his … [lung cancer was well-treated,] it again reminded me how faith … [can plant] hope in people.” 

    Pope Leo’s recovery from cancer also influenced younger followers of the Christian community. 

    “[In the Christian Church,] we always learn to believe in God even when we have no idea what will happen in the future … which is … [a little] scary,” Ethan Lee (11) said. 

    Furthermore, many reflected on how their religious belief can persevere  despite uncertainty.

    “Seeing how…[Pope Leo] went through such hardship, I think faith and belief … gives people something positive to hold on to, … reminding us to not stop praying for those who struggle with illness,” said Lee. 

    Despite returning from recovery, the Vatican confirmed the Pope will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov. 6 -17. Considering these plans, Maria has concerns.

     “I’m just worried if his health would deteriorate from this busy schedule,” Maria said. “[I mean,] he just came back.”

    She reflects on the significance of the Pope’s return.

    “His recovery truly did encourage and showed us … [the] importance of prayer and compassion … not only to our Catholic Church community, but to the world,” Maria said.

    About the Contributors
    Ella Kang, Staff Writer
    Beginning her belated journey in journalism as a senior in high school, Ella Kang is jubilant to initiate her very first step into the grand journalism industry through the Falconer as a Staff Writer. Alongside journalism, her panoramic history as a writer includes distinct genres such as fiction, poetry and nonfiction. With her flaming love towards fantasy, she has won a few awards with her short stories and poems, all while she is also in the process of publishing her very first research paper on psycholinguistics. Indeed, her interests do not end at the edge of the meager black ink. Beyond writing, she adores her moments as a dog-walker, a teacher, a singer and a lover of her friends and family. She currently has two jobs — a dog-walker of her own community and an all-rounder at a small poke-bowl shop in the Del Mar Highlands Towncenter — while accelerating her skills as an educator at two different nonprofit organizations, serving as an English teacher for more than 50 students. With these multiplexed shades, Kang is looking forward to transforming the Falconer into a treasure.
    Jaewon Jang, Graphics and Multimedia Editor
    Diving into his last year as a high school student, Jaewon Jang keeps his determination to make brilliant graphics for the Falconer. Overcoming his immigration challenges and settling as a proud member of the Falconer staff, he is more than excited to proceed into a new year of the Falconer with both old and new members incoming. Besides his role as a Graphics Editor, Jang is often found in his house or at the beach, enjoying observing nature. His primary interest outside of the Falconer is scientific research and biology study; he is a member of the TPHS Biology Olympiad Club and the leader of the Biology Books club. With his past experiences from various situations and his continuous effort to keep his creativity improved, Jang will continue his career, aiming to share his insight with other staff members.
